overall: The AG found the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: two members on the June 23 site visit were not a quorum, and the June 26 letter was scheduling information sent by the agent, not deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission deliberated without notice before and during a June 23, 2013 site visit that led to an encounter at the complainant's property.
allegations.key_passage: Because a quorum of the Commission is three members and only two members were present, no deliberation occurred on June 23, 2013, and therefore no meeting requiring a posted agenda and minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged two members who appeared at the property were not authorized to represent the Commission because no agenda or minutes showed a vote empowering them.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission's failure to produce an agenda and minutes of a meeting allowing the two members present on June 23, 2013 to represent the Commission does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission improperly deliberated before mailing a June 26, 2013 letter telling him it would discuss work on his property.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we find that the letter dated June 26, 2013 was not the product of improper deliberation.
